rationale: C24 plausibly supplied a material template for the child. Both are personal presidential letters thanking a senior defense figure for distinguished service while emphasizing that the recipient will remain available in an advisory capacity. The child closely adapts C24's distinctive pairing of gratitude for past service with appreciation for service or counsel still to come. C23 and C10 share commendatory language, including “job well done,” but lack the same past-service/continuing-advice structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I want you to know how much I appreciate all that you have done, as well as all that you will do in the future as a consultant and adviser.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: For all that you have done in your country's behalf and for the service which you will continue to give out of your abundant experience, I tender you heartfelt assurance of my gratitude and appreciation.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel construction combines appreciation for completed service with anticipated future service, changing Forrestal's continuing advice and counsel into Eisenhower's role as consultant and adviser.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The nation is extremely fortunate to have had the benefit of this most recent service by you.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Your service to your country covering a period of almost nine years during this administration and that of my predecessor has been as varied as it has been distinguished.
shared_material.explanation: Both letters frame the recipient's work as distinguished national service before delivering the President's thanks.

shared_material.child_excerpt: As President of the United States and as Commander-in-Chief, I want to thank you for a difficult job well done.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: You discharged all these duties well and faithfully.
shared_material.explanation: Both culminate in a direct presidential commendation for successful performance of demanding defense responsibilities.
